text:
Alex Kim: Heads-up — we just saw a lane-level latency spike in eu-west dedicated pool E on host rack-7, looks like one tenant's NVMe+MLPrep jobs are saturating the egress and dragging down small inference tails.
Priya Rao: ugh, saw similar from telemetry. KPIs: p50 steady but p95/jitter up ~350ms for short chat calls. Any quick isolate ideas? :thinking_face:
Matt H.: Can we soft-quarantine that tenant to a fractional slice and pin other latency-sensitive tenants off that NIC? We have fractional carveouts but haven't applied per-tenant NIC shaping in eu-west yet.
Alex Kim: I'd prefer routing fallback first — move latency-sensitive requests to the warm hotlane (low-concurrency small-instance pool) rather than carving, to avoid prefill costs. But routing will add cross-AZ hops for some customers.
Priya Rao: Cost note: hotlane has +10% cost on GPU hours but reduces p95 by ~60ms historically. If we push too many, warm pool could hit fill and cause cold-starts. Tradeoff.
Matt H.: Proposed plan: 1) soft-route 25% of affected tenant traffic to hotlane for 10m canary 2) if p95 improves, expand to 50% and concurrently apply NIC egress shaping to tenant's host slices 3) if no improvement, force carveout to dedicated fractional slice.
Laura C.: Sounds good. Can infra-bot create the canary config and alert on cold-start count?
infra-bot: Canary created: canary_id=canary-eu7-2026-03-23-01. Routing rule applied to 25% with weighted-proxy. Alert thresholds: p95>200ms OR cold_starts>5 in 10m.
Alex Kim: Rolling out now. Adding a quick debug hook — please watch this query for tail latency: `select time, p95_ms from inference_metrics where pool='eu-west-dedicated-E' and tenant='tenant-mlprep' order by time desc limit 50;`
Priya Rao: Initial 5 minutes: p95 still high on original lane, hotlane p95 ~70ms. No cold starts yet.
Matt H.: I'm kicking NIC shaping on the suspected hosts (rack-7 nodes 03..07). Command: `ssh ops@rack-7-n03 sudo /opt/rdw/bin/egress-shape --tenant tenant-mlprep --rate 150mbps`
Laura C.: Noted. Remember to keep shaping window at 5m then step down if we see error rate increase.
infra-bot: Shaper jobs started on nodes n03,n04,n05,n06,n07. Job IDs: shaper-7791..7795. ETA for stabilization: ~90s.
Alex Kim: Within 90s p95 on the dedicated lane dropped ~120ms. Hotlane remains stable. Good sign.
Priya Rao: Observed a tiny uptick in 429s from tenant-mlprep (~0.2%) since shaping — within expectation, monitor.
Matt H.: If 429s creep, we should fallback 100% of their traffic to preemptible pool until long jobs finish. Preemptible is cheaper but has jitter; ok for their batch pipelines.
Laura C.: Who owns the cost hit if we route a bunch to hotlane? We need a temporary chargeback note to billing.
Alex Kim: I'll log a quick billing ticket. Short term I think infra covers emergency mitigation; long-term we'll scope rate-limits in tenant contract.
Priya Rao: Post-mortem items noted: - automated noisy-tenant detection (add NVMe iops + egress correlate) - per-region NIC shaping rollout - routing policy weight fallback matrix tuning - cost chargeback runbook
Matt H.: Also add a test in preflight to simulate NVMe+egress combos so we can catch this in staging.
infra-bot: Canary canary-eu7-2026-03-23-01 status: PASS. p95 improved by 45% on impacted traffic. Canary will auto-scale up to 50% routing over next 5m unless blocked.
Laura C.: Great. Create follow-up thread for carved-out scheduling if we need to go that route. Thanks team :party_parrot:
Alex Kim: Thanks — I'll keep monitoring and update if anything regresses.
Priya Rao: Thx, all.
Matt H.: Leaving logs here for oncall: `https://telemetry.redwood/graphs?view=eu-west-dedicated-E&tenant=tenant-mlprep&range=15m`
Laura C.: Logged billing ticket #BILL-9812.
Alex Kim: Closing thread if no regressions in 30m.
Priya Rao: agreed.
